items.excerpt: ## House GOP Blocks Impeachment Charges Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 11, 2026 House Republicans on Tuesday blocked impeachment charges against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. By a margin of just seven votes, Republicans managed to bury the charges in committee through a 211-204 party-line procedural vote. Eleven Democrats skipped the vote, including Democratic Congressmember Nancy Pelosi of California. While House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is vying for the speakership in January, expressed support for Hegseth’s impeachment, many wondered how it was such a surprise that he was unable to corral Democratic votes to impeach Hegseth. items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 11
items.excerpt: 11 November 2026• Update: 11 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Wednesday, including US House blocking effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi "very productive." The US House of Representatives on Tuesday voted 211-204 to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort. Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it. Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out extrajudicial killings in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen. Hegseth dismissed the effort at a Pentagon news conference earlier Tuesday. - COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus World leaders are set to gather in Türkiye’s Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday for a two-day summit at the COP31 UN climate conference, with the Turkish presidency putting electrification at the center of its push to turn climate pledges into action. Türkiye is seeking support for a proposal to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. Turkish Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are scheduled to address the opening session at the Antalya Expo Center at 12.15 p.m. local time (0915GMT). National statements are due to begin at 2.30 p.m. and continue Thursday. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks, is among those expected to speak Wednesday, along with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are also expected to address the summit. - US Secretary of State Rubio describes Abu Dhabi talks between US, Russia, Ukraine as 'very productive' US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterized trilateral negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive," saying their diplomatic efforts are looking to construct durable security arrangements. "There's a lot of work to be done in that regard. It's not like something that's on the verge of being solved in the next 24 hours or anything like that," Rubio told reporters at a G7 ministerial meeting in France. Rubio said Russian representatives agreeing to the trilateral format and showing up is "good."

items.title: Fed officials open door to a quicker round of rate hikes as inflation worsens | live
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller's comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025. By mid-morning, market pricing reflected about a 15% chance of a half-point rate hike before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. Over the course of the day, traders also piled into bets the Fed would keep to its usual quarter-point rate hikes but deliver three of them by mid-2027, rather than two as seen before the data. ... The October data showed unexpected jumps in the cost of auto insurance, public transportation and medical services, increases that could land particularly hard on middle- and lower-income households. Policymakers see those groups as the weak link in an overall solid consumer spending picture. ... He said the data put the core Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index on track to rise 0.34% in October, which would translate into a 4% annualized pace and represent an increase from the prior month. The Fed uses the PCE Price Index to measure progress toward its 2% inflation target, but it considers the core figure a better measure of inflation trends. ... Before becoming the mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Haymitch was a tribute from District 12. Director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson cast a then-19-year-old Joseph Zada as Haymitch. Zada impressed with his charisma and mischief, essential for the role. The film's production spanned five months across Spain and Germany. The series has a lasting cultural impact, with over 100 million books sold and $3.3 billion in box office revenue. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also return in the epilogue. ... Jordan Firstman has been a lot of things, but 'Club Kid' confirms he's a filmmaker NEW YORK (AP) — It’s taken some time but Jordan Firstman, with “Club Kid,” feels like he’s finally made it. Since its debut at the Cannes Film Festival, “Club Kid” has been a sensation. Now, he just needs to stay on his game. The film, which Firstman wrote, directed and stars in, draws from Firstman's own experiences with gay nightlife. His character is hard-partying, hard-drug user who's shocked to discover he has a 10-year-old son. After a bidding war, A24 picked it up for $17 million and is releasing the film in the heart of awards season. Firstman has been a provocative viral-video star, a TV series writer, an actor and more. But “Club Kid” confirms he's a filmmaker. ... German period drama “The Empress” has been a big hit outside of Europe. ... Broadway finds its Prince: Jordan Fisher cast as 'The Kid' in 'Purple Rain' musical NEW YORK (AP) — Jordan Fisher will star in the Broadway adaptation of “Purple Rain” as “The Kid.” The musical is set to premiere next spring at the Majestic Theatre, with previews starting in March. Additional casting details will be announced later. “Purple Rain” tells the story of a rising rock musician in Minneapolis who's dealing with a challenging home life and a new romance. The film's soundtrack, featuring hits like “Let’s Go Crazy” and “When Doves Cry,” won two Grammys. This role marks Fisher's first original Broadway role. Prince, who inspired the story, died in 2016. Walliams and Brand were leading UK comics. Now they are part of a reckoning over sexual misconduct LONDON (AP) — A day after British actor-comedian Russell Brand was sent to prison for rape and sexual assault, allegations have surfaced against another leading comedian, David Walliams. The cases have sparked a wider reckoning about celebrity misconduct in the U.K. Walliams, a feted children's author and well-known TV personality, is facing allegations of using his fame to exploit young female fans. He had sought to block news organizations from publishing these claims, but a judge dismissed his bid. Walliams has not been charged, but the revelations have prompted questions about the media and entertainment industries' roles in enabling such behavior. Authorities are now urging stronger protections for women.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 11 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: Kabaddi 5: After the Final Match has passed Rs 12 crore at the domestic box office, with Film Development Board figures released on 9 November 2026 putting its gross at Rs 12,39,92,245 from 405,884 tickets as of 8 November 2026. Lalibazar still leads the domestic collections in the Film Development Board’s latest figures, published on 9 November 2026: Rs 93.2 million after 51 days in cinemas, ahead of Roll No. 1 at Rs 17.4 million and I Am Jit Bahadur at Rs 3.1 million. The figures cover Lalibazar, now into its second month on release. ## Remembering Toukie Smith has died aged 74. The model and actress, who played Eva Rawley on 227 and appeared on Miami Vice, died on 4 November 2026 in a New York hospital after a long battle with multiple sclerosis, her twins Airyn and Julian confirming her death to The Hollywood Reporter. Diewait Ikpechukwu, the veteran Nollywood actor and former footballer known for playing traditional rulers, has died aged 71 after a prolonged illness. He died on 5 November 2026, and the death was announced the following day by Abubakar Yakubu, National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria. ## Trailers and first looks HBO’s three character posters for Harry Potter give each of the young leads the same treatment: Dominic McLaughlin as Harry, Arabella Stanton as Hermione and Alastair Stout as Ron, wands held upright down the centre of the frame under the line “The first year begins”. The motion versions carry a first snippet of Hans Zimmer’s score, and the eight-episode first season, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, premieres on 25 December 2026 on HBO and HBO Max. Disney and National Geographic have announced The Real Frozen, a natural history series in which Idina Menzel, Kristen Bell and Jonathan Groff return to narrate, with Josh Gad making special appearances as Olaf. It will air on National Geographic and Disney+, and no premiere date has been announced. Salman Khan shared the official trailer for Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace online on 10 November 2026. The war drama, inspired by the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash and directed by Apoorva Lakhia, opens in cinemas on 4 December 2026. The theatrical trailer for Gunmaaster G9 is due out today, 11 November 2026, ahead of the Emraan Hashmi romantic action film’s cinema release on 27 November 2026. Danny Boyle’s Ink, a drama about the birth of The Sun newspaper, has a new trailer, with Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch and Jack O’Connell as Larry Lamb. It opens in UK and Ireland cinemas on 8 January 2027. Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut also has a new trailer, starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti alongside Halle Bailey, ahead of its theatrical release on 11 December 2026. Dario Russo’s comedy The Fox follows the same pattern, its new trailer putting Jai Courtney and Emily Browning front and centre, with Olivia Colman and Sam Neill in one of his final performances, for a 4 December 2026 cinema release. Mouli’s dark comedy DNK, about robbery and crime, has its trailer out ahead of a 13 November 2026 cinema release. Ravi Teja launched the trailer. ... First reviews for Steps, Netflix’s animated Cinderella reimagining starring Ali Wong as Lilith, landed on 9 November 2026 and run mostly favourable: three of the four reviews quoted are positive, with The Hollywood Reporter dissenting. It streams on Netflix from 20 November 2026.

items.title: NEW MUSIC: QUEEN Releases QUEEN BUDAPEST Concert Film Soundtrack and HUDSON STONE, BEHEMOTH!, EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE Singles
items.excerpt: The release includes a newly remixed soundtrack from the original multitrack, with new music from HUDSON STONE also featured. By: Rachel Stone Nov. 11, 2026 ... Sony Music Vision presents Queen Budapest, the first Western stadium rock show behind the Iron Curtain and the final filmed Queen live performance, in new formats. The Queen Budapest soundtrack, newly remixed from the original multitrack by Queen's studio team, is also available now. ... In the U.S. and Canada, the soundtrack is released via Hollywood Records as a 3LP, 2CD and digital release. Internationally, it is available via Sony Music in Blu-ray, DVD, CD and digital editions, and as a 3LP vinyl set for the first time. Last month, Queen Budapest was released globally in cinemas and IMAX to critical acclaim. ## Hudson Stone Releases 'Talk - Live From the Worlds Collide Concert Tour' Video Hollywood Records artist Hudson Stone celebrated his 15th birthday last week with the release of 'Talk - Live From the Worlds Collide Concert Tour,' a new performance video capturing the energy of his first arena tour. Filmed across multiple stops on the Worlds Collide Concert Tour, the video puts Stone's guitar-driven sound and dynamic stage presence front and center, offering fans a closer look at the rising artist as he performs for arena audiences across North America. ## BEHEMOTH! Original Motion Picture Soundtrack Hollywood Records and Searchlight Pictures release the BEHEMOTH! Original Motion Picture Soundtrack on Friday, November 13. It features original music by The Behemoth! Collective: Michael Abels, Emily Bear, Lukas Frank, Michael Giacchino, James Newton Howard, Henry Jackman, Nami Melumad, Brandon Roberts and Alan Silvestri. Each composer wrote as the voice behind a different piece of music in the story, from a blockbuster franchise score, a vintage cartoon theme to a cello etude and a talented young composer's original songs. The film was written and directed by acclaimed filmmaker Tony Gilroy and stars Pedro Pascal as Alex Serian, a cellist who returns to Los Angeles after 20 years on the road. The vinyl edition is available to pre-order now at Disney Music Emporium. ## Everest: The Other Side Original Motion Picture Soundtrack Hollywood Records and National Geographic release the Everest: The Other Side Original Motion Picture Soundtrack, with music by Caroline Ho, on Friday, November 13.
